Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Las Vegas NV
915 PM PST Mon Nov 16 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Precipitation and cooler weather arrives Monday and lasts
  through Tuesday

* Gusty southwest to west winds are expected Tuesday into Tuesday 
  evening for much of the area. 

* A colder system arrives in the mid-week, causing Winter Storm
  Watch for the Eastern Sierra for accumulating snow and bringing 
  another batch of scattered showers for the rest of the region.

&&

.DISCUSSION...Through Monday

A cold front is currently making its way south along the Sierra 
Nevada and is expected to reach the Eastern Sierra this afternoon. 
Most of the precipitation will remain along the western slopes of 
the Sierra, although a few isolated light showers will be possible 
overnight across portions of southern Nevada and southeast 
California. As the trough continues to dig over the eastern Pacific, 
it will tap into some Pacific moisture overnight into Tuesday. While 
this moisture tap is not particularly impressive, PW values are 
expected to increase to 200-250% of normal for this time of year 
across the CWA. As the trough begins to swing inland late tonight 
into Tuesday, improving dynamics, including strong upper-level 
diffluence, will combine with the increasing moisture to support 
scattered to widespread showers across mainly the eastern half of 
the forecast area, including Clark, Lincoln, and Mohave counties.
The greatest potential for heavier rainfall and isolated 
thunderstorms will be across Lincoln and Mohave counties, where WPC 
has outlined a Marginal Risk for excessive rainfall. Rainfall totals 
will generally range from 0.25 to 0.50 inches across these areas, 
with amounts elsewhere remaining below 0.25 inches. While locally 
heavier showers could result in isolated flooding, the overall flood 
risk remains low.

Gusty southwest to west winds are also expected late tonight through 
Tuesday, with most areas seeing sustained winds of 15 to 25 mph and 
gusts around 30 mph. However, stronger winds are expected across 
southern Clark County and northern San Bernardino County, including 
the I-15 corridor, where sustained winds of 20 to 30 mph and gusts 
around 50 mph are likely. A Wind Advisory has been issued for these 
areas Tuesday morning through Tuesday afternoon. Winds will decrease 
and shift to the northwest behind the cold front, although Esmeralda 
and central Nye counties could still see gusts of 30 to 35 mph 
Tuesday afternoon and evening.

After a brief break on Wednesday, a stronger and wetter system is 
expected to push into the West Coast. While this system is not 
expected to dig as far south as Tuesday's trough, it will feature a 
more substantial moisture tap, with strong IVT values supporting 
significant precipitation across the Sierra Wednesday night through 
Thursday. Current snowfall forecasts call for 10 to 18 inches 
between 5,000 and 8,000 feet, with 18 to 36 inches above 8,000 feet 
and locally higher amounts along the Sierra crest. Strong winds will 
accompany the snowfall, with gusts exceeding 50 mph along the 
highest peaks.

Although the bulk of the moisture will remain focused on the Sierra, 
some precipitation will spread into the remainder of the CWA. This 
could bring lighter snow accumulations to the higher elevations of 
southern Nevada, including around 4 inches at Mt. Charleston, along 
with another round of rain showers that could linger into early 
Friday. Rainfall rates are expected to remain relatively light, but 
the prolonged duration of precipitation could result in storm totals 
of 0.10 to 0.40 inches across much of the region.

There is still some uncertainty regarding the timing of this system, 
as the trough is currently located over the Gulf of Alaska and model 
guidance is beginning to suggest a slower progression inland near 
the California/Oregon border. As a result, adjustments to the timing 
and precipitation amounts may be needed in subsequent forecasts. 
Beyond Friday, a transient ridge is expected to build over the 
region, keeping additional precipitation farther north while 
allowing temperatures to gradually warm through the weekend.

&&

.AVIATION...For Harry Reid...For the 06Z Forecast Package...Light 
winds expected through the early morning hours with decreasing CIGS 
as light shower activity moves into the Las Vegas Valley. Heavier 
showers with CIGS of 3-5kft AGL are expected after 8z with mountain 
obscuration expected. Improving conditions expected near sunrise 
with increasing southwesterly winds and gusts of 20-25 knots. Sky 
conditions will improve through the day with fairly rapid clearing 
expected through the morning hours. Winds will trend light by the 
evening. 

For the rest of southern Nevada, northwest Arizona and southeast 
California...For the 06Z Forecast Package...Winds across the region 
will be somewhat variable through the evening, with speeds generally 
around 5 to 10 knots. Light showers will continue to overspread the 
area overnight, which may potentially bring CIGs down to 2kft to 
4kft AGL at times. Improving conditions are expected Tuesday 
morning, with most of the shower activity moving east of regional 
terminals by late morning with fairly rapid clearing from west to 
east. Winds will trend light areawide by early evening. 

&&

.SPOTTER INFORMATION STATEMENT...Spotters are encouraged to report
any significant weather or impacts according to standard operating
procedures.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Gorelow/Murdock 
AVIATION...Planz

For more forecast information...see us on our webpage:
https://weather.gov/lasvegas or follow us on Facebook and Twitter
